relevance_note: A WES cohort of 80 children with unexplained liver disease; one cohort member is described individually: 'One patient with Familial Behçet-Like Autoinflammatory Syndrome caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation received infliximab treatment'.
method_note: Read manually; no table transcribed by script. Only one in-scope person (the single TNFAIP3 case in Group A); the other 79 cohort members are out of scope (cohort_size_as_stated = 80; 216 enrolled before exclusions). The paper gives this person no label, so 'unnamed person 1' (label rule 6; not a case report). Variant details are only in Supplementary Table 1 and Figure 2, which are not in the Markdown, so the variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported' and no zygosity, inheritance or ACMG class. Cohort-level statements were applied to this person: consanguinity 'no' ('No consanguineous marriages were found in the cohort.'), vital status 'alive' ('All patients survived during the follow-up'), and ethnicity 'Chinese' ('in a Chinese pediatric population'). The methods say WES was done in patients and their parents, but no parental result is given for this patient and the paper notes parental samples were not always available, so parental_testing_statement and inheritance are 'not reported'. Exclusion criteria (autoimmune hepatitis, viral and other infections) were not used to mark any feature. Group A membership (liver enzyme elevation group) was used as evidence of elevated liver enzymes; absence of cholestasis was not inferred from the grouping rule. No checklist item is addressed for this person; all 20 are 'not reported'. Contradictions in the paper (none about this person): 46 patients with genetic results vs Figure 2 legend '45 children'; Discussion says 57.5% (46/80) carried P/LP variants while Results say P/LP variants in 42/80; Methods say written consent was obtained from at least one parent while the IRB statement says consent was waived.
